Hi Jordan — thanks for the great conversation. Quick recap and our proposed next steps below. I attached a short process diagram (redwood-rtbf-process.pdf) and example DPA redlines for your legal team.

Recap (end-to-end):
- Request intake: Customer submits RTBF via API or support portal. Requests create a ticket and are routed to our compliance queue.
- Soft-delete: We immediately mark all primary records as deleted (soft-delete) across the active serving data stores; this makes data logically inaccessible to application queries within minutes.
- Hard purge (primary stores): For primary storage (active databases / object stores) we perform a physical purge during the next background sweep job. Typical window: 24-72 hours after soft-delete, depending on shard/partition state.
- Backups & snapshots: Backups are immutable. We rely on regular backup snapshot rotation for removal. Typical policy: 30-90 day snapshot retention depending on customer tier and region. For Hosted customers, standard is 30 days; Dedicated/Private customers can configure longer windows. Because snapshots are immutable, we cannot surgically remove an item from an existing snapshot — purge is achieved by waiting for the snapshot to age out.
- Logs: Operational logs and request traces that contain user identifiers are stored separately and have a configurable retention. Default retention: 90 days. We can reduce retention to meet stricter compliance needs (minimum 30 days) subject to monitoring and troubleshooting trade-offs.

Exceptions / constraints:
- Immutable backups: As noted, deletion from historical backups requires waiting for snapshot expiry; we can provide attestations and an export showing when objects were removed from primary stores and when backups rotated.
- Third-party processors: If a customer opts to replicate to a third-party analytics/store, deletion obligations extend to configured integrations.

SLA / timing options we can offer:
- Standard hosted: primary purge 24-72 hours, backups removed on 30-day rotation.
- Priority (enterprise add-on): primary purge within 24 hours, expedited snapshot rotation (30-day max for backups) and formal attestation within 10 business days.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm desired backup retention window and whether you require expedited rotation/attestation (Jordan).
2) If needed, we will add a clause in the SOW/contract for expedited rotation and a deletion attestation (Marissa will draft).
3) Provide sample API call and response for RTBF intake (Alex will attach a small example).

Attachments: redwood-rtbf-process.pdf; example-dpa-redlines.pdf

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick follow-up if you want to review the MP and SOW language.

Looping in some implementation detail. Jordan — quick clarifications from the infra side: 

- Backups: our standard managed snapshots are weekly (full) with daily incrementals. For hosted customers the net effect is a 30-day retention window by default; that means worst-case data may persist in an older snapshot until the snapshot containing the data rolls out of the retention window. We can offer an expedited rotation for enterprise customers (contract-level) which enforces a 30-day hard max and provide a signed attestation when the object is no longer present in primary stores and the snapshot index shows removal.

- Expedited deletions: For Dedicated/Private deployments we can provide tooling and runbooks to perform an on-demand snapshot rebuild / re-encryption and scrub, but this requires maintenance window and is scoped as a professional service (PS) engagement.

- Logs: we can scope log scrubbing for IDs (hashing/anonymization) if you need to preserve logs for operations while removing PII. That is often the best compromise for auditability.

Next internal steps: Alex — can you attach the sample API payload and the internal runbook excerpt so we can send them to Jordan? I’ll start a draft SOW clause for expedited rotation.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Infrastructure Security
